cards.front: What were the main problems facing the Weimar Republic 1919-1923?
cards.back: Treaty of Versailles (war guilt, reparations, territory loss), Spartacist Uprising, Kapp Putsch, Hyperinflation 1923, Invasion of Ruhr.

cards.front: What was the 'Stab in the Back' myth (Dolchstosslegende)?
cards.back: Right-wing claim that German army didn't lose WWI but was betrayed by politicians ('November Criminals') who signed armistice.

cards.front: What caused hyperinflation in 1923?
cards.back: Government printed money to pay striking workers in Ruhr (passive resistance). More money chasing fewer goods = prices skyrocketed.

cards.front: How did Stresemann solve hyperinflation?
cards.back: Introduced Rentenmortgage (new currency), ended passive resistance in Ruhr, negotiated Dawes Plan (US loans, reduced reparations).

cards.front: What was the Dawes Plan (1924)?
cards.back: US loans to Germany (800M marks), reparations reduced, French/Belgian troops leave Ruhr. Kickstarted 'Golden Years'.

cards.front: What was the Young Plan (1929)?
cards.back: Reduced reparations to £1.85B over 59 years. Right-wing opposed (Hugenberg, Hitler campaigned against it).

cards.front: How did the Wall Street Crash (1929) affect Germany?
cards.back: US loans recalled. German banks/collapsed. Unemployment rose to 6M by 1932. Government cut spending/wages. Nazi votes surged.

cards.front: Why did Hitler become Chancellor in January 1933?
cards.back: Largest party in Reichstag (37%), Hindenburg/Papen thought they could control him, conservative elite wanted Nazi support, no viable alternative.

cards.front: What was the Reichstag Fire (Feb 1933)? How did Hitler use it?
cards.back: Parliament building burned. Communist van der Lubbe blamed. Hitler got Hindenburg to sign 'Decree for Protection of People and State' - suspended civil liberties, banned communists.

cards.front: What was the Enabling Act (March 1933)?
cards.back: Allowed Hitler to pass laws without Reichstag for 4 years. Passed 444-94 (Centre Party supported). Legal basis for dictatorship.

cards.front: What happened on Night of the Long Knives (June 1934)?
cards.back: Hitler purged SA leadership (Röhm) and political rivals. SS/Gestapo killed ~85-200. Army swore oath to Hitler. Consolidated power.

cards.front: How did Nazis control the police state?
cards.back: Gestapo (secret police), SS (Heinrich Himmler), concentration camps, informers, block wardens, courts controlled, opposition banned.

cards.front: How did Goebbels control propaganda?
cards.back: Minister of Propaganda. Controlled press, radio, film, theatre, art, music. Rallies (Nuremberg), censorship, 'Strength Through Joy', cheap radios (Volksempfänger).

cards.front: What was the Nuremberg Laws (1935)?
cards.back: Anti-Jewish laws: Reich Citizenship Law (Jews not citizens), Law for Protection of German Blood (banned marriage/relations with Aryans). Defined 'Jew' by grandparents.

cards.front: What was Kristallnacht (Nov 1938)?
cards.back: 'Night of Broken Glass'. SA/SS attacked Jewish homes, shops, synagogues. 91 killed, 30,000 to camps. Jews fined 1 billion marks. Escalation of persecution.

cards.front: How did Nazis reduce unemployment?
cards.back: Public works (autobahns), rearmament (conscription 1935), RAD (labour service), invisible unemployment (women/Jews removed from stats), excluded from official figures.

cards.front: What was Nazi policy towards women?
cards.back: Kinder, Küche, Kirche (Children, Kitchen, Church). Encouraged motherhood (Mother's Cross medals), banned from professions, limited university places, Law for Encouragement of Marriage (loans).

cards.front: What was the Hitler Youth? What did they do?
cards.back: Compulsory from 1939. Boys: military training, fitness, ideology. Girls (BDM): domestic skills, motherhood prep. Indoctrination in Nazi beliefs.

cards.front: How did Nazis control education?
cards.back: Curriculum changed: Race studies, PE increased, History (Nazi version), Biology (eugenics). Teachers in Nazi Teachers' League. Textbooks rewritten. Jewish teachers dismissed.

cards.front: Evaluate: 'The main reason Hitler consolidated power was the Enabling Act.'
cards.back: Agree: Legal basis for dictatorship, bypassed Reichstag. Disagree: Reichstag Fire Decree came first (suspended rights), Night of Long Knives removed internal opposition, Army oath secured military loyalty. All interconnected.
